describe.title: Create an agent
describe.subtitle: What should it be for? One job, said plainly.
describe.placeholder: Watch the performance budget on every pull request, and comment with the regression when a page gets slower.
describe.hint: An agent with one job is an agent whose runs you can read. Two jobs in one definition is two agents.

suggestions.perfBudget: Watch the performance budget on every pull request
suggestions.changelog: Keep the changelog in step with what merged
suggestions.triage: Triage new issues and label them

describe.notRegister: This is not Register an agent. Register wraps an agent that already runs on a machine or in CI, and it starts from Register an agent on the Agents page. This writes one that does not exist yet.

identity.title: Identity
identity.subtitle: The slug is fixed once the pull request merges. Everything the agent does is attributed to the key it ends.
identity.slugHint: The file is .oxagen/agents/{slug}.toml, and the slug is the last part of the agent key. It never changes once the pull request merges.
identity.slugInvalid: Use lowercase letters, digits, and single hyphens, up to 18 characters.
identity.harnessHint: The harness this agent is written for. Oxagen generates the subagent file from the definition, in the same pull request.
identity.tierHint: A tier, not a model id. The route behind it belongs to the organization and can change without touching this file.

definition.title: The definition
definition.subtitle: .oxagen/agents/{slug}.toml. Every field on the agent page is a view of this file.

drafted.title: A definition, drafted from what you wrote
drafted.body: Oxagen filled a template in from your description, in this tab. No model wrote it and no run was recorded. Every line below is yours to change before anybody reviews it.

file.header:
The definition is the record. Nothing here is written to a database by the wizard:
the definition is published when a person merges this pull request. Register the agent afterward to create its identity.
file.stayInside:
Work inside the toolbelt you were given. When a step needs authority you do
not hold, stop and say which one. Do not route around it.

definition.otherSlug: the file says {slug}, the identity step says {expected}
definition.tools: {count, plural, one {# tool pattern} other {# tool patterns}}
definition.request: tools is a request, not a grant. What the agent can reach is this list intersected with the roles it holds and with your own grants, never wider than either.
definition.invalidSlug: Set slug to a lowercase name with hyphens, up to 18 characters.

toolbelt.title: The toolbelt
toolbelt.subtitle: What the definition asks for. A role grant is what hands it over.
toolbelt.label: Tools in this workspace’s registry
toolbelt.search: Pick a tool by its name or slug
toolbelt.empty: The tool registry of this workspace holds no tools yet. Import one or declare one on the Tools page. Until then the definition asks for the fallback belt.
toolbelt.denied: Reading the tool registry needs a workspace role. You can still continue: the definition asks for the fallback belt.
toolbelt.unavailable: The tool registry could not be read ({code}). You can still continue: the definition asks for the fallback belt.
toolbelt.more: This is the first 100 tool versions. Add any other by name in the definition.
toolbelt.nothing: Nothing picked. The definition falls back to search_graph and recall_memory, a belt that reads the graph and memory and writes nothing.
toolbelt.noneParks: Nothing on this belt parks. Every tool picked is a read or a reversible write, so runs finish without waiting on a person.
toolbelt.someParks: {count, plural, one {# of these parks for a person.} other {# of these park for a person.}} A call to an irreversible or high-risk tool stops at the gateway and waits for an approver, every time, until somebody writes an auto-approval rule for it.
toolbelt.handEdited: You changed the definition by hand, so the belt picked here is not written into it. Revert the file on the previous step to let these picks through.

pr.title: Open the pull request
pr.subtitle: An agent is a definition in a repository before it is a principal in a database.
pr.lead: Merging this publishes the definition of {slug} in {workspace}. After merge, register it under the same slug to create its identity.
pr.fileGenerated: generated from the definition, read by Claude Code, Cursor, and stella
pr.codex: Codex documents no subagent file, so the pull request writes none for it.

schema.name: Schema
schema.detail: agent-definition/v0.1, and the slug in the file matches the file name

key.name: Key
key.detail: no other agent in this workspace holds the slug, live or retired

belt.name: Belt
belt.detail: every pattern in tools resolves to a tool in the registry or a capability; a pattern that resolves to nothing fails

authority.name: Authority
authority.detail: no irreversible side effects, which need a mandate, and nothing wider than your own grants

budget.name: Budget
budget.detail: per_run_micros is set; an agent with no budget cannot start a run

secrets.name: Secret and PII scan
secrets.detail: the whole file is scanned, and a literal credential fails the check

repo.unbound: This workspace has no main repository yet. Bind one in Workspace settings, then open the pull request.
repo.denied: Opening an agent pull request needs Owner or Admin on the organization.
repo.unavailable: The main repository could not be read ({code}). Nothing was written. Close the wizard and open it again to retry.

opened.title: Pull request opened
opened.subtitle: Register the agent after its definition merges.
opened.proposed: {slug} is proposed. After merge, register it under the same slug to create its identity and credential.
opened.register: After the merge, create its identity and credential with Register an agent on the Agents page, under the same slug.

failure.checkSchema: The schema check failed: the file must parse, declare agent-definition/v0.1, carry the slug from the identity step, and name its model tier, tools, and instructions. Nothing was written.
failure.checkKey: The key check failed: another agent in this workspace already holds this slug. Go back and choose another. Nothing was written.
failure.checkBelt: The belt check failed: a pattern in tools resolves to no tool in the registry and no capability. Nothing was written.
failure.checkAuthority: The authority check failed: the file asks for irreversible side effects, or for a tool you do not hold. Nothing was written.
failure.checkBudget: The budget check failed: set budget.per_run_micros to a whole number above zero. Nothing was written.
failure.checkSecrets: The secret scan found a credential or personal data. Remove it and try again. Nothing was written.
failure.orgRoleRequired: Opening an agent pull request needs Owner or Admin on the organization.
failure.noRepository: This workspace has no main repository yet. Bind one in Workspace settings.
failure.githubRefused: GitHub refused the write. Check the GitHub App’s access to the repository and try again.
failure.gitlabRefused: GitLab refused the write. Nothing was published. Check that the project access token still has the api scope and the Developer role, then try again.
failure.gitlabCredentialRejected: GitLab no longer accepts the project access token stored for this project. Nothing was changed. Connect the project again with a new token.
failure.unanswered: Oxagen did not answer. Nothing was written. Try again.
failure.refused: The pull request was refused ({code}). Nothing was written.
failure.invalid: The {field} value is not one propose_agent accepts. Nothing was written.
failure.pendingApproval: Opening this pull request waits for approval: access request {request}.
